name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
short_description: 5th-century palace on top of a 200 m rock, with frescoes, the Lion Gate and water gardens.
description: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century as a fortified palace on a granite column rising about 200 m above the plain. The climb passes landscaped water gardens, the famous cloud-maiden frescoes, the Mirror Wall and the giant lion paws before reaching the palace ruins on the summit. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the most iconic sight in Sri Lanka.
best_time_to_visit: Opening time (7:00) or late afternoon; January to April for the clearest weather
tips: Start early to avoid the midday heat and the crowds.
Bring water; there is no shop on the summit.
Photos of the frescoes are not allowed.
Climb neighbouring Pidurangala for the classic view of Sigiriya itself.

name: Pidurangala Rock
short_description: Short, steep climb past a reclining Buddha to the best viewpoint of Sigiriya.
description: Pidurangala is a rock next to Sigiriya with an old cave temple and a large reclining Buddha. The final section is a scramble over boulders. From the top you get a panoramic view of Sigiriya rising out of the jungle, especially beautiful at sunrise.
tips: Wear shoes with grip for the final boulder scramble.
Cover shoulders and knees when passing the temple at the base.
Bring a torch if you go for sunrise.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
short_description: Five painted cave shrines filled with over 150 Buddha statues, a UNESCO site.
description: The Dambulla cave complex has been a place of worship for over 2,000 years. Five caves under a huge overhanging rock contain Buddha statues and colourful ceiling paintings. A climb of a few hundred steps leads up from the golden temple at the road.
tips: Shoes must be removed; the rock can be very hot at midday.
Cover shoulders and knees.
Watch your bags around the monkeys.

name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
short_description: Medieval royal capital with well-preserved ruins and the Gal Vihara rock carvings.
description: Polonnaruwa was the second capital of Sri Lanka (11th–13th century). The compact site includes the royal palace, the Quadrangle with its round Vatadage, and Gal Vihara, four Buddha figures carved from one granite wall. Easy to explore by bicycle.
tips: Rent a bicycle in town to move between the ruins.
Visit the museum first; it explains the layout of the city.
Remove shoes and hats at shrines.

name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
short_description: Sri Lanka's first capital: giant stupas and the sacred Sri Maha Bodhi tree.
description: Anuradhapura was the capital for over a thousand years and is still an active pilgrimage site. Highlights include the white Ruwanwelisaya stupa, the brick Jetavanaramaya (one of the tallest ancient structures in the world) and the Sri Maha Bodhi, grown from a cutting of the tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning; Poya (full moon) days are busy with pilgrims
tips: Wear white or light clothing that covers shoulders and knees.
The site is large; hire a tuk-tuk or a bicycle.
Socks help on hot stone when shoes are off.

name: Minneriya National Park
short_description: Home of 'The Gathering', where hundreds of elephants meet around the reservoir.
description: Minneriya is centred on an ancient reservoir. In the dry season (roughly July to October) large herds of wild elephants come to graze on the grass of the shrinking lake, one of the biggest elephant gatherings in Asia. Jeep safaris start from Habarana.
tips: Ask your driver whether Minneriya, Kaudulla or Hurulu Eco Park has the most elephants that day.
Jeep hire is paid separately from the park ticket.
Keep noise down and never ask the driver to get too close.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
short_description: Kandy's most sacred temple, home of the Buddha's tooth relic.
description: The Sri Dalada Maligawa in Kandy houses the relic of the tooth of the Buddha and is the most important Buddhist shrine in the country. Daily puja ceremonies with drummers draw crowds of devotees. In July/August it is the centre of the Esala Perahera festival.
best_time_to_visit: During the morning or evening puja
tips: Strict dress code: cover shoulders and knees; no hats.
Shoes are left at a counter outside.
Never pose with your back to a Buddha image for photos.

name: Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya
short_description: Large, beautiful gardens near Kandy with orchids, giant bamboo and a fig tree avenue.
description: Founded in 1843, the gardens cover about 60 hectares on a bend of the Mahaweli River. Highlights are the orchid house, the palm avenues, the spice garden and the giant Javan fig tree.
tips: Easy to combine with a visit to Kandy.
Bring an umbrella; afternoon showers are common.

name: Nine Arch Bridge
short_description: Colonial-era railway viaduct in Ella surrounded by jungle and tea.
description: This stone-and-brick viaduct near Ella was completed in 1921 and is one of the most photographed spots in Sri Lanka. Watching a blue train cross the nine arches is a highlight. It is a short walk from Ella town.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning, timed with a train
tips: Check the train timetable locally; trains are often late.
Do not walk on the tracks when a train is approaching.

name: Little Adam's Peak
short_description: Easy walk through tea plantations to a ridge with views over Ella Gap.
description: A gentle hike of about 45 minutes from Ella through tea estates to a grassy summit with panoramic views of the hills and Ella Rock. Suitable for most fitness levels.
tips: Good first hike in Ella.
Clouds often roll in after midday.

name: Ella Rock
short_description: Harder half-day hike along the railway and up through forest to big views.
description: Ella Rock is a more challenging hike than Little Adam's Peak. The trail follows the railway line, then climbs through eucalyptus forest. The path is not always clear, so many travellers hire a local guide.
best_time_to_visit: Start at dawn, January to April
tips: Use an offline map or a guide; wrong turns are common.
Ignore people who claim the trail is closed and offer a 'shortcut' for money.

name: Horton Plains & World's End
short_description: High plateau with a 9 km loop to the World's End cliff and Baker's Falls.
description: Horton Plains National Park is a cool, misty plateau at over 2,000 m. A 9 km loop trail leads to World's End, a sheer drop of about 870 m, and the pretty Baker's Falls. Sambar deer are often seen.
best_time_to_visit: Arrive at opening (6:00); clouds often cover World's End by 10:00
tips: Bring warm layers; it is cold in the early morning.
Plastic is checked at the gate.
Stay overnight in Nuwara Eliya or Ohiya to arrive early.

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
short_description: Night pilgrimage of about 5,500 steps to watch sunrise from a sacred summit.
description: Sri Pada (2,243 m) is sacred to Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims and Christians because of a footprint-shaped mark at the top. Pilgrims climb through the night from Dalhousie to reach the summit for sunrise and see the peak's triangular shadow.
best_time_to_visit: Pilgrimage season, December to May; start around 2:00
tips: Outside the season the tea shops and lights along the path are closed.
Bring warm clothes for the summit.
Weekends and Poya days are extremely crowded.

name: Nuwara Eliya & Tea Estates
short_description: Cool colonial hill town surrounded by tea plantations and factories to visit.
description: Nicknamed 'Little England', Nuwara Eliya has colonial buildings, a lake and a cool climate. Nearby tea factories such as Pedro Estate offer tours where you see how tea is processed and can taste it.
best_time_to_visit: January to April; April is busy with local holidaymakers
tips: Nights are cold; pack a jumper.
Tea factory tours usually charge a small fee.

name: Galle Fort
short_description: Walled Dutch colonial town with ramparts, cafés, boutiques and a lighthouse.
description: Built by the Portuguese and expanded by the Dutch in the 17th century, Galle Fort is a living town inside massive ramparts. Walk the walls at sunset, explore narrow streets of colonial houses, churches, mosques and small museums.
best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to sunset on the ramparts; December to April
tips: Walking the ramparts is free.
Dress modestly when entering churches and mosques.

name: Unawatuna Beach
short_description: Sheltered bay near Galle, good for swimming and snorkelling.
description: Unawatuna is a curved, reef-protected bay just south of Galle, with calm water in season, beach restaurants and the Japanese Peace Pagoda on the headland. Nearby Jungle Beach is quieter.
tips: Swim only between the flags; currents get strong in the monsoon.

name: Mirissa
short_description: Laid-back beach town and the main base for blue whale watching.
description: Mirissa has a palm-fringed beach, Coconut Tree Hill viewpoint and a lively evening scene. From roughly November to April, boats leave early in the morning to look for blue whales, sperm whales and dolphins.
tips: Choose a whale-watching operator that respects distance rules.
Take seasickness tablets before the boat trip.

name: Yala National Park
short_description: Sri Lanka's most famous safari park, with a high density of leopards.
description: Yala in the south-east is known for leopards, elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles and many birds. Block 1 is the busiest; other blocks are quieter. The park usually closes for part of September and October.
tips: Stay in Tissamaharama or Kirinda to be at the gate for opening.
Jeeps crowd around leopard sightings; a quieter block may be better.
Check closure dates before planning.

name: Udawalawe National Park
short_description: Open grassland park where elephants are seen on almost every safari.
description: Udawalawe surrounds a large reservoir and has open terrain, which makes elephants easy to spot all year. Next to the park, the Elephant Transit Home cares for orphaned calves before releasing them.
best_time_to_visit: All year; early morning or afternoon
tips: Visit the Elephant Transit Home at feeding time.
Good stop between the south coast and Ella.

name: Gangaramaya Temple
short_description: Eclectic Buddhist temple and museum in central Colombo.
description: Gangaramaya mixes Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian and Chinese architecture and holds a curious collection of donated objects. Nearby, the Seema Malakaya pavilion floats on Beira Lake.
best_time_to_visit: Morning or evening; very busy during Vesak
tips: Cover shoulders and knees.
The ticket usually also covers Seema Malakaya.

name: Galle Face Green
short_description: Seafront promenade in Colombo, best at sunset with street food.
description: A long oceanfront lawn in the heart of Colombo where families fly kites and street-food stalls sell isso wade (prawn fritters) and kottu in the evening.
tips: Try isso wade from the stalls.
The sea is not safe for swimming here.

name: Bentota
short_description: Long golden beach with river safaris and water sports, close to Colombo.
description: Bentota has a wide beach and a river lagoon where you can take mangrove boat trips. It is known for resort hotels, water sports and Geoffrey Bawa's garden at Lunuganga nearby.
tips: Visit the turtle hatcheries in Kosgoda nearby; choose ethical ones.

name: Trincomalee & Nilaveli
short_description: Natural harbour, Koneswaram temple and white-sand Nilaveli beach with Pigeon Island.
description: Trincomalee has one of the world's finest natural harbours and the clifftop Koneswaram Hindu temple. North of town, Nilaveli beach is the base for snorkelling trips to Pigeon Island National Park.
tips: Pigeon Island has its own park fee.
Dress modestly at Koneswaram.

name: Arugam Bay
short_description: Sri Lanka's top surf spot, with a relaxed village atmosphere.
description: Arugam Bay has world-class right-hand point breaks and spots for beginners. Outside the surf there are lagoon safaris and Kumana National Park to the south.
tips: Many businesses close outside the season.
Take surf lessons at Whiskey Point or Baby Point if you are a beginner.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil, Jaffna
short_description: The most important Hindu temple in Jaffna, with a golden gopuram.
description: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is dedicated to Lord Murugan and is the heart of Tamil Hindu culture in Jaffna. Its annual festival (around July–August) lasts 25 days and attracts huge crowds.
tips: Men must remove shirts before entering.
Photography inside is not allowed.
